Exercise: Elevated Back Lunge

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_lower_body

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- glutes
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- glute_activation
- quadriceps_strength

Contraindications:

- condition: knee injury, description: May exacerbate knee issues.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Reverse Lunge, mechanic: unilateral lower body
- name: Single-Leg Deadlift, mechanic: unilateral lower body

Substitution Options:

- name: Dumbbell Lunge, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Position a bar onto a rack at shoulder height loaded to an appropriate weight. Place a short, raised platform behind you.
- Rack the bar onto your upper back, keeping your back arched and tight. Step onto your raised platform with both feet. This will be your starting position.
- Begin by stepping backwards with one leg. Descend by flexing your hips and knees until your knee touches the floor.
- Pause, and extend through the hips and knees to rise up, returning all the way to the starting position before alternating.
